entries.sense_en: easy to notice; standing out from the people around

synonyms.nuance: Neutral and everyday: can be seen or heard, without suggesting it stands out strongly.
Stands out because of position or importance, often positively.
Obvious in a bad way: shameless, with no attempt to hide it.

entries.tip_ko: 'be conspicuous by one's absence'(없어서 오히려 눈에 띄다)라는 표현으로도 자주 쓰입니다.

entries.sense_en: short and sharp in shape; here, cut short, like a small pointed beard

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for small length; says nothing about tone or neatness.
Trimmed neatly and closely; for hair, hedges or speech.
Describes speech or manner that is abrupt and slightly rude, not shape.

entries.tip_ko: 보통은 '말이 퉁명스러운'이라는 뜻으로 쓰이고, 여기서는 수염이 짧게 깎였다는 드문 용법입니다.

entries.sense_en: guessed something without proof; supposed

synonyms.nuance: Everyday, informal; can be a quick unsupported answer.
Formal; a guess based on some clues, often about a hidden fact.
synonyms.example: They surmised he had left town.

synonyms.nuance: Think and talk about possibilities at length, often with no firm ground.

entries.tip_ko: 여기서는 수동태(it was conjectured that ...)로, 격식체 문장에서 자주 나옵니다.

entries.sense_en: a state of great excitement, confusion and worry

synonyms.nuance: Complete disorder with no control; not necessarily emotional.
Noisy, short-lived excitement, usually in a crowd.
A big, lasting disruption to a settled situation.

entries.sense_en: a person of enormous size or great power in some field

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for a huge person or a leading figure.
synonyms.example: a giant of the film industry

synonyms.nuance: Literary; a powerful leader, often in business or industry.
Something huge and heavy, often a company or a machine; less admiring.

entries.tip_ko: 원래 '거대한 조각상'(로도스의 거상)이라는 뜻에서 나왔습니다.

entries.sense_en: in an extremely tiny way, too small to measure

synonyms.nuance: Formal; in very small detail or amount (stress on the second syllable: my-NOOT-ly).
Plain adjective; doesn't have the 'too small to measure' feeling.
Small enough to need a microscope; a more literal picture of size.

entries.tip_ko: in-fi-ni-TES-i-mal-ly: 강세는 'tes'에 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: skill and quickness in using the hands or the mind

synonyms.nuance: General word for ability gained by practice; not focused on hands or speed.
Neat, quick and light handling; close to dexterity but less formal.
Quick, light movement of the whole body or mind.

entries.sense_en: a state where nothing moves, changes or develops

synonyms.nuance: Calm and quiet, often pleasant; stagnation suggests something unhealthy.
Plain word for not doing anything; no bad-smell feeling of decay.
Movement or progress has stopped completely, perhaps temporarily.

entries.sense_en: dug up out of the ground; here, moles pulled out of their holes

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrasal verb; any digging out of the ground.
Formal; specifically to dig up a dead body, e.g. for an investigation.
Find something hidden, in the ground or in records; often figurative.

entries.sense_en: old, worn and in poor condition from long use

synonyms.nuance: Damaged by use, but doesn't say it looks poor or untidy.
Untidy and unkempt; often said of people, clothes or pets.
Usually a building or area in bad condition through neglect.

entries.tip_ko: 사람의 행동에 쓰면 '비열한'이라는 뜻도 됩니다 (a shabby trick).

entries.sense_en: pleasantly odd and old-fashioned

synonyms.nuance: Pleasing in general; doesn't suggest old-fashioned or odd.
Pretty enough to be painted; about scenery and places.
Strange, with no charm implied; can be negative.

entries.sense_en: got off a train or bus at the end of a journey

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrasal verb; used for any vehicle.
Formal; leave a ship, plane or train, often many passengers at once.
Get down from a horse or bicycle, not a train.

entries.tip_ko: alight는 '불이 붙은'이라는 형용사로도 쓰입니다 (The house was alight).

entries.sense_en: a raised platform; here, one side of the square standing higher than the others

synonyms.nuance: General word for any raised flat surface, including in stations.
A small stand for one speaker or conductor to stand on.
Raised area for performers in a theatre or hall.

entries.tip_ko: 보통 '데이이스'로 발음하며, '다이어스'(/ˈdaɪəs/)로 읽는 사람도 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: plain and ordinary, lacking imagination or wonder

synonyms.nuance: Simply boring; no suggestion of lacking poetry.
Boring because of daily routine and sameness.
Practical and unemotional, sometimes a good quality.

entries.sense_en: two events happening together by chance in a surprising way

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for luck or accident; no idea of two things matching.
Informal; a lucky accident, often a good result.
Literary; chance circumstance, often in the phrase 'by happenstance'.

entries.tip_ko: '우연히'는 by coincidence, 또는 문장으로 What a coincidence!

entries.sense_en: to a degree too deep to understand or measure
entries.sense_ko: 헤아릴 수 없을 만큼, 이루 말할 수 없이

synonyms.nuance: Plain intensifier; no idea of being impossible to understand.
Too great to measure; about amount or degree.
In a way that cannot be understood.

entries.tip_ko: 형용사 unfathomable(헤아릴 수 없는)에서 온 부사이며, 여기서는 '뼛속까지'처럼 강조하는 말로 쓰였습니다.

entries.sense_en: slow, steady and unexciting, but thorough

synonyms.nuance: Careful, orderly and systematic; entirely positive.
Needing much hard, tiring effort; stresses the effort.
Stubborn and never giving up.

entries.sense_en: a statement so obviously true that it hardly needs saying

synonyms.nuance: An overused phrase or idea; the stress is on being stale, not true.
A dull remark said as if it were wise.
A basic principle accepted as true, used as a starting point.

entries.sense_en: complete lack of knowledge; not knowing anything

synonyms.nuance: Common word for lack of knowledge, often with blame.
Not knowing that something exists or is happening.
Figurative and literary; here, being 'in the dark' about something.

entries.tip_ko: nescience는 문어체 희귀어입니다. 일상 영어에서는 ignorance를 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: an arranged meeting place

synonyms.nuance: Plain, neutral description.
A secret place to hide, not merely to meet.
Literary; a secret meeting of lovers.

entries.tip_ko: 프랑스어에서 온 말로 단수는 끝의 s가 소리 나지 않지만, 여기처럼 복수로 쓰이면 철자는 같고 /ˈrɑndeɪvuz/로 발음합니다.

entries.sense_en: a street closed at one end, with no way through

synonyms.nuance: Most common everyday phrase; also used figuratively for a plan going nowhere.
A narrow passage closed at one end; often used for hopeless situations.
British street name form for a short residential road with one end closed.

entries.tip_ko: 프랑스어로 '자루의 바닥'이라는 뜻이며, 오늘날 주택가의 막다른 길을 가리킬 때 흔히 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: to act without any plan or reason for the choice

synonyms.nuance: In a careless, disorganized way; suggests no order at all.
Without seeing or knowing enough to choose well.
Based on whim, not on reason or rule; often criticizing a decision.

entries.tip_ko: at random(무작위로)은 pick at random처럼 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: usual, proper and following the accepted way

synonyms.nuance: Following common custom; neutral and everyday.
Handed down from the past; stresses history.
The normal, usual type; no sense of rules or belief.

entries.tip_ko: Orthodox Church(정교회)처럼 종교에서도 쓰이지만, 여기서는 '보통의'라는 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: become boring after being repeated many times

synonyms.nuance: Idiomatic; a joke or excuse slowly loses its effect.
Directly makes someone uninterested; needs an object and no idea of repetition.
Make someone weary, physically or mentally.

entries.tip_ko: 'pall on 사람' 구조로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a person who acts or moves more slowly than others

synonyms.nuance: Informal, American; someone who is annoyingly slow.
Someone who wastes time or lingers when they should move.
synonyms.example: a dawdler on the way to school

synonyms.nuance: Formal; someone who falls behind others.

entries.tip_ko: 영국식 표현이며, 여기서는 slow coach의 비교급입니다.

entries.sense_en: rude boldness that shows no respect

synonyms.nuance: Informal; shameless boldness, as in 'What a nerve!'
Formal; disrespect toward someone who deserves respect.
Strong; bitter, shocking boldness.
synonyms.example: the gall to ask for more

entries.tip_ko: '뺨'이라는 뜻 외에 '뻔뻔함'(What a cheek!)이라는 영국식 뜻이 있습니다. confounded는 '괘씸한' 정도의 옛 강조어입니다.

entries.sense_en: look at something very closely and carefully

synonyms.nuance: General word for checking something carefully.
Check officially or for faults.
Look at for a long time to learn, with less suspicion.

entries.tip_ko: 영국식 철자 scrutinise가 쓰였고, 미국식은 scrutinize입니다.

entries.sense_en: a sign or card with writing on it, put up for the public

synonyms.nuance: General word for any board or card with information.
Written information posted to be read.
Larger printed sheet, often with a picture.

entries.sense_en: a threatening feeling or look

synonyms.nuance: The more common word; a warning or danger, spoken or not.
Open unfriendliness and anger; not necessarily a threat of harm.
The possibility of harm, not tied to a person's attitude.

entries.tip_ko: '골칫거리'라는 뜻으로도 쓰입니다 (a menace to society).

entries.sense_en: heavy and slow-moving because of size

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for great weight; no idea of slowness or clumsiness.
Moving slowly and awkwardly, like a big animal.
Awkward and likely to knock things over; size not required.

entries.tip_ko: 말이나 글에 쓰면 '지루하고 장황한'이라는 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: watch carefully so as not to miss anything

synonyms.nuance: Everyday; watch for something as one goes along.
synonyms.example: Keep an eye out for the bus.

synonyms.nuance: Actively searching for a particular thing or danger.
Remain attentive in general, not for one object.

entries.modern: keep an eye out (또는 keep your eyes peeled)
entries.tip_ko: keep one's eyes peeled라고도 하며, 오늘날에는 peeled 쪽이 훨씬 흔합니다.

entries.sense_en: dirty, wet and untidy, as if dragged through mud

synonyms.nuance: The usual modern form; wet, dirty and limp.
Dirty in a small, everyday way; not necessarily wet or limp.
Old and worn out, rather than dirty and wet.

entries.sense_en: loud and vulgar in a way that is impossible to ignore

synonyms.nuance: Shockingly obvious, said of wrongdoing or breaking rules.
Bold and shameless, showing no embarrassment.
Too bright and colourful in bad taste; about looks only.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날에는 blatant lie(뻔뻔한 거짓말)처럼 나쁜 행동에 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: grand and richly decorated, like a palace

synonyms.nuance: Impressive in size or style; a common everyday word.
Very comfortable and expensive; not necessarily large.
Showing great wealth, sometimes too much.

entries.sense_en: a hint or clue that shows what to do next

synonyms.nuance: A fact that helps solve a mystery; used for finding out the truth.
A sign that tells someone to act, often deliberate.
A small, indirect suggestion.

entries.tip_ko: 원래 연극에서 배우가 다음 대사를 시작하는 신호를 뜻합니다. 발음은 'clue'와 달리 /kju/입니다.

entries.sense_en: a great shock or surprise

synonyms.nuance: Sudden, shocking news that changes things.
Plain word for a sudden surprise, good or bad.
Informal; something surprisingly impressive or shocking.

entries.tip_ko: 권투의 KO에서 나온 비유로, 여기서는 웨이터가 받은 충격을 나타냅니다.

entries.sense_en: calmly and without any concern

synonyms.nuance: Plain adverb; quietly and without worry.
Calm and slightly unfriendly or unmoved.
Casually, as though it did not matter at all.

entries.tip_ko: 옛 속어로 'All serene!'은 '좋아, 문제없어'라는 뜻이었습니다.

entries.sense_en: too bright and colourful in a cheap way

synonyms.nuance: Bright and showy in poor taste; very close to garish.
Showy to attract attention, often to display wealth.
Positive or neutral; full of colour without any criticism.

entries.tip_ko: '가리쉬'가 아니라 /ˈɡɛrɪʃ/(게어리시)로 발음합니다.

entries.sense_en: so great and grand that it fills you with awe

synonyms.nuance: Grand and dignified, like a king or a mountain.
Wonderful and splendid; a broader word of praise.
Bright and admirable; often about weather, victories and light.

entries.tip_ko: 여기서는 하늘의 영광과 대조하려고 '숭고한 저속함(sublime vulgarity)'이라는 역설적인 표현을 썼습니다.

entries.sense_en: a habit of bending the head and shoulders forward

synonyms.nuance: Lazy, careless sitting or standing with drooping shoulders.
Bend the back, often from cold or worry.
General word to curve the body; no sense of a habit.

entries.tip_ko: 미국에서 stoop은 집 앞의 작은 계단을 뜻하기도 합니다.

entries.sense_en: a person new to something who is easy to fool

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; someone new to a skill or job.
Informal, American; a beginner, especially in sports or police work.
Old-fashioned; someone not used to rough outdoor life.

entries.sense_en: too ready to believe anything, so easy to trick

synonyms.nuance: Lacking experience of life; not always about being fooled.
Formal; too willing to believe things.
Positive or neutral; ready to trust people.

entries.sense_en: any sensible explanation or logic

synonyms.nuance: Reasoned thinking behind something.
A good, practical reason.
The purpose of an action.

entries.tip_ko: 보통 'without rhyme or reason'(아무 이유 없이)처럼 부정문으로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: thought very hard to find an answer

synonyms.nuance: Think about something confusing for a while.
Older, more violent version of the same idiom.
Think slowly and deeply; calmer than racking.

entries.tip_ko: rack이 전통적인 철자이며(고문 도구 '형틀'에서 유래), wrack으로 쓰는 경우도 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: an animal or person being hunted or chased

synonyms.nuance: An animal hunted for food; more about nature than sport.
Something aimed at; no idea of chasing.
Someone harmed; has no sense of being hunted.

entries.tip_ko: '채석장'이라는 뜻으로 더 자주 쓰이지만 여기서는 사냥 용어입니다.

entries.sense_en: badly made or in bad repair and likely to fall apart

synonyms.nuance: Shaky and weak, especially of furniture or stairs.
Damaged from neglect; usually a house or car.
Partly fallen down; mainly buildings.

entries.sense_en: a puzzling, mysterious subject that is hard to understand

synonyms.nuance: Something unexplained; the more general word.
A puzzle with a clever answer, often a game.
A problem to work out; can be a toy or game.

entries.sense_en: a person who does not believe in the speaker's religion

synonyms.nuance: Neutral term for someone without religious faith.
Old, insulting; someone outside Christianity or any major religion.
Someone who firmly believes there is no God; not an insult.

entries.tip_ko: 지금은 모욕적일 수 있어 현대 영어에서는 거의 쓰지 않습니다.

entries.sense_en: a vague, in-between place at the edge of things

synonyms.nuance: Land or area between two regions or states.
synonyms.example: the borderland between sleep and waking

synonyms.nuance: Disputed empty ground between two sides.
synonyms.example: the no man's land between the trenches

synonyms.nuance: A state of being forgotten or unaware.

entries.tip_ko: in limbo는 '어중간하게 결정이 나지 않은 상태'로 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: an imaginary stone of extreme hardness, like a fantasy diamond

synonyms.nuance: The real hardest natural stone.
A hard metal, used for strength.
A hard rock used for building.

entries.tip_ko: 'adamant'는 흔히 '단호한'(형용사)으로 쓰이지만 여기서는 옛 명사 용법입니다.

entries.sense_en: give something to someone, especially when told to

synonyms.nuance: Stop keeping something; can be unwilling.
Give up completely to a stronger force.
Give casually, like at a table.

entries.tip_ko: 'Hand it over!'는 도둑이나 경찰이 쓰는 명령형 표현이기도 합니다.

entries.sense_en: solemn and self-important, like a bishop or pope

synonyms.nuance: Full of self-importance in speech; more general and negative.
Serious and dignified; not necessarily showing off.
Showing off moral goodness and looking down on others.

entries.sense_en: a high-ranking church official such as a bishop

synonyms.nuance: A specific rank in charge of a diocese.
Any member of the clergy, high or low.
Ordinary religious leader conducting services; lower than a prelate.

entries.tip_ko: 여기서는 플랑보가 상대를 비꼬아 부르는 말입니다.

entries.sense_en: not married and not having sexual relations, as a priest

synonyms.nuance: Just not married; no promise of abstaining.
Avoiding sex outside marriage or entirely; moral tone.
Everyday word for having no partner.

entries.sense_en: a clever trick used to cheat or avoid something

synonyms.nuance: General word for a clever act, playful or dishonest.
A clever plan to deceive; slightly formal.
A dishonest scheme to get money.

entries.tip_ko: 동사 dodge는 '피하다'이지만, 이 문장에서는 명사입니다.

entries.sense_en: a person who confesses sins to a priest

synonyms.nuance: Someone who has done wrong; no idea of regret.
The priest who hears confession, the opposite role.
Adjective for someone truly sorry.

entries.tip_ko: 형용사로는 '뉘우치는'이라는 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: practical common sense and boldness

synonyms.nuance: Ability to act without being told.
Courage to do something risky.
Quick intelligence in tricky situations.

entries.tip_ko: 구어체에서 '기민한 판단력과 용기'를 칭찬할 때 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a junior priest who helps a parish priest

synonyms.nuance: The priest in charge of a parish in the Church of England.
A priest serving an institution such as a hospital or army.
General term; not necessarily junior.

entries.tip_ko: 동사 curate(전시를 기획하다)와는 발음도 뜻도 다릅니다.

entries.sense_en: an awkward, unsophisticated person from the countryside

synonyms.nuance: Mocking; a simple country person.
American, insulting; ignorant rural person.
A poor farm worker in the past; the insult means rude or uncultured.
